stories.why_ar: داخلك اثنان، والذي تُطعمه هو الذي يكبر.
lines: An old man was talking to his grandson.
"There is a fight inside me," he said. "It is between two wolves."
"One wolf is anger, envy and fear."
"The other is peace, hope and patience."
"The same fight is inside you, and inside every person."
The boy thought for a long time.
Then he asked, "Which wolf wins?"
The old man was quiet.
"The one you feed," he said.
The boy never forgot that answer.
stories.moral_ar: ما أطعمتَه فيك كبِر، وما تركتَه ضعُف.

stories.why_ar: أكثر ما يوقفنا ليس الحبل، بل ما تعلّمناه عنه صغاراً.
lines: A man walked past some elephants and stopped.
Each huge animal was held by a thin rope on one leg.
There was no chain and no cage.
The elephants could break the rope in one second, but they did not try.
He asked their keeper why.
"When they are very small," the keeper said, "we use the same rope."
"At that age it is enough to hold them."
"They pull and pull and cannot get free."
"They grow up believing the rope is stronger than they are."
"So they never try again."
stories.moral_en: We are held by what we believe, not by what is true.
stories.moral_ar: ليس الحبل هو الذي يمسكك، بل اعتقادك أنّك لا تقدر.

stories.why_ar: قد يكون الذي لا تراه أهمّ ممّا تراه.
lines: A farmer planted a bamboo seed and watered it every day.
In the first year nothing came out of the ground.
In the second year, nothing again.
His neighbours laughed at him in the third year.
In the fourth year, the ground was still empty.
He kept watering it anyway.
In the fifth year a small green plant appeared.
In six weeks it grew twenty metres tall.
"Did it grow in six weeks?" a neighbour asked.
"No," said the farmer. "It grew for five years. We could not see it."
stories.moral_en: Roots grow before anything else does.
stories.moral_ar: ما لا يظهر في الأرض هو الذي يحمل ما يظهر فوقها.

stories.why_ar: لا تحكم على اليوم قبل أن ترى الغد.
lines: A farmer's horse ran away one night.
"What bad luck!" said the neighbours. "Maybe," said the farmer.
A week later the horse came back with three wild horses.
"What good luck!" they said. "Maybe," said the farmer.
His son tried to ride one of them and broke his leg.
"What bad luck!" they said. "Maybe," said the farmer.
The next month, soldiers came to the village.
They took every young man for the war.
They did not take the son with the broken leg.
"What good luck!" said the neighbours. And the farmer smiled.
stories.moral_en: You cannot judge a day by its morning.
stories.moral_ar: لا تعرف خير الأمر من شرّه حتى يتمّ.

stories.why_ar: ما تظنّه عيبك قد يكون أجمل ما فيك.
lines: A man carried water every day in two pots on a stick.
One pot was perfect. The other had a crack.
The cracked pot arrived home only half full.
For two years it felt ashamed.
One day it said, "I am sorry. I lose half your water."
The man said, "Did you see the flowers on your side of the path?"
"There are none on the other side."
"I knew about your crack, so I planted seeds there."
"Every day you watered them as we walked."
"For two years I have picked those flowers for my table."
stories.moral_en: Your crack is where something else can grow.
stories.moral_ar: من أحسن استعمال نقصه جعله موضع الزهر.

stories.why_ar: ما يُرمى عليك يمكن أن يصير الدرج الذي تصعد عليه.
lines: A farmer's donkey fell into an old dry well.
The animal cried for hours.
The well was deep and the farmer could not pull him out.
In the end he decided to fill the well with earth.
The neighbours came with spades and began to throw earth in.
The donkey cried louder — then he went quiet.
The farmer looked down, surprised.
With every spade of earth, the donkey shook it off his back.
Then he stepped up on it.
Higher and higher, until he walked out over the edge.
stories.moral_en: Shake it off and step up.
stories.moral_ar: انفض ما أُلقي عليك، ثم قف فوقه.

stories.why_ar: العمل واحد، والفرق كلّه في جواب «لماذا».
lines: A traveller passed three men cutting stone in the sun.
He asked the first man, "What are you doing?"
"I am cutting stone," he said, without looking up.
He asked the second man the same question.
"I am earning money for my family," he answered.
He asked the third man.
The man stood up and looked at the hill.
"I am building a cathedral," he said.
All three were doing exactly the same work.
Only one of them was tired at the end of the day, and it was not the third.
stories.moral_en: The same work feels different when you can see the building.
stories.moral_ar: من رأى البناء لم يتعب من الحجر.

stories.why_ar: المعاناة التي تُختصر لك قد تُفقدك جناحيك.
lines: A man found a cocoon on a branch and watched it for hours.
A small hole appeared, and a butterfly began to push out.
It pushed for a long time and did not move forward.
The man felt sorry for it.
He took scissors and cut the cocoon open.
The butterfly came out easily.
But its body was fat and its wings were small and wet.
The man waited for the wings to open.
They never did, and the butterfly could not fly.
The hard push through the hole is what sends the blood into the wings.
stories.moral_en: The struggle is not in the way; it is the way.
stories.moral_ar: الجهد الذي تظنّه عائقاً هو الذي يفتح الجناح.

stories.title_en: The Blind Men and the Elephant
stories.why_ar: كلّهم صادق، وكلّهم لم يرَ إلا جزءاً.
lines: Six blind men wanted to know what an elephant was like.
The first touched its side. "It is a wall," he said.
The second held the tusk. "No, it is a spear."
The third took the trunk. "You are both wrong. It is a snake."
The fourth felt a leg. "It is a tree."
The fifth touched an ear. "It is a fan."
The sixth held the tail. "It is a rope."
They argued loudly for a long time.
Every man was telling the truth about the part he touched.
And every man was wrong about the elephant.
stories.moral_en: Part of the truth is not the truth.
stories.moral_ar: من أمسك طرفاً وظنّه الكلّ، صدَق في طرفه وأخطأ في حكمه.

stories.why_ar: أحياناً الفرق الوحيد بين النجاة والغرق هو أن تستمرّ دقيقةً أخرى.
lines: Two frogs fell into a deep pot of cream.
The sides were smooth and they could not climb out.
"This is the end," said the first frog.
He stopped moving his legs, and he went down.
The second frog did not answer.
He kicked, and kicked, and kicked.
His legs hurt and the night was long, but he kept kicking.
Slowly the cream under him began to change.
By the morning it had turned into butter.
The frog stood on it and jumped out.
stories.moral_en: Keep moving; the ground can change under you.
stories.moral_ar: من لم يكفّ عن الحركة صنع بحركته أرضاً يقف عليها.
